forecast Drivers
forecast Drivers · 4 records
  1. Automotive unit volume, price/mix, credits and regional incentives; battery supply limits and vehicle affordability matter.
  2. Energy deployment is lumpy and revenue recognition differs from GWhdeployments; tariffs/warranty costs can reverse gross-margin gains.
  3. Services/other grows with installed fleet, insurance, charging, used cars and FSD; not all service revenue has software margins.
  4. Robotaxi, Cybercab and Optimus need explicit geography, intervention/safety, paid utilization, fleet/customer and margin milestones before major base-case cash flows.
accounting And Cash Notes
accounting And Cash Notes · 4 records
  1. Keep SBC in EBIT;2025 and 2026 CEO award expense/restricted share issuance require separate dilution reconciliation.
  2. Space X mark-to-market gain is below operating income and is not recurring vehicle/energy profit.
  3. Q 2 revenuegrew 26%whileoperatingmarginwas 1.4%; higher revenue alone does not establish AI business profitability.
  4. Cash Capex>25 bn guide is gross cash spending, not delta revenue/S:C net reinvestment. Working capital and depreciation bridge required.

    Keep the stated early investment intensity, then apply the disclosed normalization path where present. Fade the final years to terminal-ROIC-consistent incremental capital efficiency so reinvestment and FCFF do not jump at the terminal boundary. This path is analytical, not company spending guidance.
    implementation Status

    simple Terminal Sales Capital From ROIC
    2.0
    terminal Capital Convention
    Explicit reinvestment uses delta revenue / S:C. Terminal reinvestment uses next-year NOPAT × g / ROIC. Therefore the matching incremental S:C is ROIC / [(1+g) × terminal margin × (1-tax)], rather than the simplified ROIC / after-tax margin ratio. Both are disclosed.

    rationale
    At the TTM mix, about 8% automotive growth and 20% energy/services growth imply about 11.2% consolidated growth. Initial 12%, 12%, 10% is an analytical recovery path. EBIT margin reaches 10%; major Robotaxi or Optimus profits are excluded. Capital efficiency must improve after the buildout.

    capital Path Rationale
    Gross cash capital-spending proxy rises34/38/42bn in years1–3, then38/35/34/34bn in years4–7; D&A rises8/11/15/20/24/27/28bn as construction is commissioned. This gradual normalization is an analytical scenario, conditional on capacity utilization and curtailing unsuccessful expansion. Years8–10 use a terminal-consistent net-investment path with explicitly derived gross-capex decomposition. No investment is claimed to disappear automatically.

    terminal Capital Convention
    Explicit reinvestment uses delta revenue / S:C. Terminal reinvestment uses next-year NOPAT × g / ROIC. Therefore the matching incremental S:C is ROIC / [(1+g) × terminal margin × (1-tax)], rather than the simplified ROIC / after-tax margin ratio. Both are disclosed.

model Gaps
model Gaps · 7 records
  1. Path-dependent CEO awards and robotaxi fleetcapital/replacement economics require separate schedules.
  2. Bearnet investmentfloorcannot be representedby current constant S:C model.
  3. Consolidated margin ramp cannot establish Robotaxi/Optimusunit economics; separatebusiness sum requiredif material.
  4. Demand, productioncapacity, deliveries, paid utilizationandrecognizedrevenuearedifferentmetrics.
  5. The selected research scenarios require early and normalized sales-to-capital ratios and, in the bear, fixed investment floors; the current single-ratio engine cannot represent them exactly.
  6. Base first3years now use direct capital/D&A/WC inputs; derived S:C is descriptive. Cash-funding view adds back noncash SBC separately from economic FCFF. Interest, legal/claims, lease credit and reserve schedules remain to be integrated.
  7. Years4–7 gross capex and D&A normalize explicitly, with strong utilization/commissioning assumptions. Year4 retaining29bn net investment instead of19.5bn is a material separate stress.

invalidation
invalidation · 4 records
  1. Automotive unit, price or mix economics fail to recover, or services fail to convert growth into EBIT.
  2. Energy deployment slows or warranty and tariff costs persist.
  3. Capex and SBC stay elevated without improved operating cash returns.
  4. Autonomy or robotics misses regulatory, safety, intervention, utilization or production milestones. Reweight the conditional bull rather than invent a quarterly guidance miss.

duration Sensitivity Definition
The six duration cases below are constant-S:C diagnostics, not the normalized-capital base. They isolate duration only.
forecast Basis
Annual rolling periods after the June 2026 TTM anchor: year one ends approximately June 2027. Calendar-2026 management guidance is a near-term reference, not mechanically the same forecast period. Post-quarter claims require a separate valuation-date bridge.
terminal Transition Policy
Final explicit S:C reconciles to forward-NOPAT terminal reinvestment. Stable growth, tax, margin and ROIC remain unchanged; terminal FCFF grows at stable g from the final explicit FCFF.

rationale
At the TTM mix, about 8% automotive growth and 20% energy/services growth imply about 11.2% consolidated growth. Initial 12%, 12%, 10% is an analytical recovery path. EBIT margin reaches 10%; major Robotaxi or Optimus profits are excluded. Capital efficiency must improve after the buildout.
valuation Status
Illustrative operating value only. Equity bridge, timing and model gaps unresolved; not a price target.
incremental Sales To Capital Early
Not specified / unresolved (null)
incremental Sales To Capital Normalized
2.0
sales Capital Normalization Year
7
capital Path Rationale
First three years use explicit timing-aware investment assumptions, with a source-anchored2026H2 bridge and analytical2027+ ranges. Later ratios remain a provisional normalization schedule, fading to terminal consistency. This is not management spending guidance.
implementation Status
Requires the explicit annual reinvestment path and any spending floors; do not substitute one fixed S:C input.
simple Terminal Sales Capital From ROIC
1.5999999999999996
terminal Capital Convention
Explicit reinvestment uses delta revenue / S:C. Terminal reinvestment uses next-year NOPAT × g / ROIC. Therefore the matching incremental S:C is ROIC / [(1+g) × terminal margin × (1-tax)], rather than the simplified ROIC / after-tax margin ratio. Both are disclosed.
terminal Capital Fade Begins After Year
7

early Capital Method

bounded Model Gaps
bounded Model Gaps · 8 records
  1. Valuation-date stub and post-anchor cash/claims/share roll-forward not integrated; this is a forecast-origin operating EV, not October 17 equity value.
  2. No probability weighting or share-price calibration. Source forecast assumptions are judgments, not reported facts.
  3. Enterprise-to-equity bridge is not computed here; consult the company-specific claim register for resolved evidence, assumptions and remaining uncertainties. Zero is not evidence of absence.
  4. Cash capital-spend guidance is not identical to economic additions; separately reconcile supplier payable changes, lease capitalization and asset commissioning.
  5. Depreciation ramps with in-service timing, useful lives and hardware replacement, not merely spending date.
  6. Cash taxes versus normalized operating taxes, interest and nonoperating income require a cash waterfall.
  7. SBC must either remain an economic expense with consistent future share treatment, or be modeled through awards/dilution consistently; no double count.
  8. A lower cash deficit does not prove attractive incremental returns.

Interest, legal payments, dividends, mandatory debt maturities, investment purchases, reserves, future award settlements beyond the stated proxy, and supplier/lease credit need a separate cash schedule. Do not deduct this deficit again as debt.
method
Start with source-anchored timing of cash capital expenditures, subtract modeled economic D&A, add core operating WC, and retain SBC in EBIT for economic FCFF. Add assumed noncash SBC only in a separate cash-funding view, then subtract separately modeled employee share-settlement cash. The 60% Meta settlement ratio is an assumption, not a repeated historical law. Actual OCF contains tax/nonoperating/working-capital timing and is not normalized FCFF.
assumptions
Rolling year1 includes >16.718bn formal-derived2026H2 floor plus an assumed15bn or greater2027H1 spend. Subsequent capex increases are scenarios informed by the public call statement that investment grows for2–3years, not quantified formal guidance. CFO borrowing-capacity intentions are not committed drawn financing.
remaining Gates

  1. Cash capital-spend guidance is not identical to economic additions; separately reconcile supplier payable changes, lease capitalization and asset commissioning.
  2. Depreciation ramps with in-service timing, useful lives and hardware replacement, not merely spending date.
  3. Cash taxes versus normalized operating taxes, interest and nonoperating income require a cash waterfall.
  4. SBC must either remain an economic expense with consistent future share treatment, or be modeled through awards/dilution consistently; no double count.
  5. A lower cash deficit does not prove attractive incremental returns.

operating Enterprise Value Illustration
3063.7718886035073
normalization Rationale
Gross cash capital-spending proxy rises34/38/42bn in years1–3, then38/35/34/34bn in years4–7; D&A rises8/11/15/20/24/27/28bn as construction is commissioned. This gradual normalization is an analytical scenario, conditional on capacity utilization and curtailing unsuccessful expansion. Years8–10 use a terminal-consistent net-investment path with explicitly derived gross-capex decomposition. No investment is claimed to disappear automatically.

interpretation
Economic core plus assumed buildout may have a near-zero or negative operating value under investment stress. This is not a complete probability-weighted equity value: curtailment, autonomy/robotics outcomes, nonoperating assets and conditional claims require separate scenarios.
cash Funding Scope
First3-year low/base/high cash-funding cases remain unchanged; full-year4+ cash waterfall, award settlements and refinancing are not claimed complete.
